content: In 1 Corinthians, speaking in tongues without love makes you like what?
explanation: Love gives meaning to gifts. “but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.” (1 Corinthians 13:1, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, faith that moves mountains without love makes you what?
explanation: Love matters most. “and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.” (1 Corinthians 13:2, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, how does Paul begin describing love?
options: Love is patient, love is kind
explanation: It does not envy or boast. “Love is patient, love is kind.” (1 Corinthians 13:4, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, which of these does love NOT do?
explanation: Love is not proud. “It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.” (1 Corinthians 13:4, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, what does love keep no account of?
explanation: Love forgives. “it keeps no account of wrongs.” (1 Corinthians 13:5, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, what does Paul say love never does?
explanation: Other gifts will pass away. “Love never fails.” (1 Corinthians 13:8, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, which three things remain?
explanation: The greatest is love. “And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love” (1 Corinthians 13:13, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, which is the greatest of faith, hope, and love?
explanation: Love never fails. “but the greatest of these is love.” (1 Corinthians 13:13, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, Paul tells believers they are the body of whom?
explanation: Each is a member of it. “Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it.” (1 Corinthians 12:27, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, whatever you eat, drink, or do, do it all to the what of God?
explanation: All of life is for God. “So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.” (1 Corinthians 10:31, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, Paul says to do everything in what?
explanation: Love guides every action. “Do everything in love.” (1 Corinthians 16:14, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, the message of the cross is foolishness to some, but what to us who are saved?
explanation: The cross saves. “but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.” (1 Corinthians 1:18, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, Paul planted and Apollos watered, but who made it grow?
explanation: Growth comes from God. “I planted the seed and Apollos watered it, but God made it grow.” (1 Corinthians 3:6, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, Paul says believers themselves are God's what?
explanation: God's Spirit dwells in them. “Do you not know that you yourselves are God’s temple” (1 Corinthians 3:16, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, since you were bought at a price, what should you do?
explanation: Your body is the Spirit's temple. “you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God with your body.” (1 Corinthians 6:20, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, Paul tells believers to run like runners in a race in order to do what?
explanation: Live with purpose. “Run in such a way as to take the prize.” (1 Corinthians 9:24, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, when you are tempted, what will God provide?
explanation: God is faithful. “But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape” (1 Corinthians 10:13, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, what did Jesus say when He broke the bread?
explanation: Do this in remembrance of Me. “This is My body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of Me.” (1 Corinthians 11:24, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, Jesus called the cup the new covenant in His what?
explanation: We remember His death. “This cup is the new covenant in My blood” (1 Corinthians 11:25, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, the body has many parts but forms how many bodies?
explanation: So it is with Christ. “And although its parts are many, they all form one body. So it is with Christ.” (1 Corinthians 12:12, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, there are different gifts but the same what?
explanation: God gives each believer gifts. “There are different gifts, but the same Spirit.” (1 Corinthians 12:4, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, when Paul became a man, what did he set aside?
explanation: Love is mature. “When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.” (1 Corinthians 13:11, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, now we see as in a mirror, but then we shall see how?
explanation: We will know fully. “Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face.” (1 Corinthians 13:12, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, on which day was Christ raised according to the Scriptures?
explanation: This is of first importance. “that He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures” (1 Corinthians 15:4, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, Paul taunts death, asking, “Where, O Death, is your…”
explanation: Christ has won the victory. “Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?” (1 Corinthians 15:55, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, what foundation has already been laid?
explanation: No other foundation can be laid. “For no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.” (1 Corinthians 3:11, BSB)

content: Who is named with Paul at the start of 1 Corinthians?
explanation: He is called our brother. “and our brother Sosthenes” (1 Corinthians 1:1, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, which name did some believers follow besides Paul, Apollos, and Christ?
explanation: Paul warned against divisions. ““I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos,” “I follow Cephas,” or “I follow Christ.”” (1 Corinthians 1:12, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, to how many brothers at once did the risen Christ appear?
explanation: Most were still living. “After that, He appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once” (1 Corinthians 15:6, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, what does Paul call the risen Christ?
explanation: Others will be raised too. “the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.” (1 Corinthians 15:20, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, at the last trumpet, how fast will we be changed?
options: In the twinkling of an eye
explanation: The dead will be raised. “in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet.” (1 Corinthians 15:52, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, where did Paul say he would stay until Pentecost?
explanation: A door for work was open. “But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost” (1 Corinthians 16:8, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, what does Paul call Christ who has been sacrificed?
explanation: So remove the old leaven. “For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.” (1 Corinthians 5:7, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, what has no eye seen and no ear heard?
options: What God prepared for those who love Him
explanation: God's plans are wonderful. “what God has prepared for those who love Him.” (1 Corinthians 2:9, BSB)

content: In 1 Corinthians, love bears, believes, hopes, and endures how many things?
explanation: Love does not give up. “It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.” (1 Corinthians 13:7, BSB)
